title: Time-lapse live-cell imaging of pyroptosis by confocal microscopy
protocol: Digest exponentially growing HEK293T cells with trypsin-EDTA to single cells.
Plate approximately 5 × 10^5 cells in 35-mm glass-bottomed culture dishes for 12–17 hours to reach 60%–70% confluency before transfection.
Discard the medium and add fresh DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS to the cells at 30 minutes before transfection.
Gently dilute the plasmid DNA (1 μg) with 50 μL serum-free DMEM.
Dilute PolyJet transfection reagent (3 μL) with 50 μL serum-free DMEM.
Mix diluted plasmid DNA and diluted PolyJet gently to prepare the transfection complex.
Incubate the mixture for 15 minutes to form the transfection complex.
Add the prepared transfection complex drop-wise to the cells and gently swirl the cell culture dishes.
Check the expression level of GSDME-NT using a fluorescence microscope after 24 hours post-transfection.

Dilute Sytox Green and Annexin V-Alexa Fluor 647 in the cell culture medium to the final concentration of 1 μM (Sytox Green) or add one drop Annexin V-Alexa Fluor 647 solution per 105 cells according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Incubate the cells with Sytox Green and Annexin V-Alexa Fluor 647 at 37°C in dark for 15 min.
Add sterile CaCl2 stock solution to the cell culture medium to reach a final concentration of 2.5 mM before Annexin V staining.
Start LSM710 confocal microscope, and pre-warm laser source.
Equip microscope with environmental control chamber.
Warm up environment chamber to 37°C, and maintain supply of humidified 5% CO2.
Place cell culture dish into the environmental control chamber.
Choose desired objective for cell imaging. Typically, 40 × (NA1.2) magnification objective is preferred.
Locate a view field of interest.
Go to the software operation panel.
Choose fluorescence channels and pseudo-colors that match the dyes used in the experiment.
Select the channel corresponding to brightfield for viewing.
Adjust the z-axis to get a clear view of interest.
Set the excitation laser power.
Optimize the gain of fluorescence to avoid low fluorescent intensity or overexposure.
Set the “Pinhole” for each fluorescent channel at 1 Airy Unit (AU).
Adjust the gain and offset of each fluorescent channel as required before imaging.
Take 512 × 512 time-lapse images at 3–5 min intervals for a total of 7 h or longer.
Save the time series images.
Represent the images as “Contents of Image window-series” or “Full resolution image window-series”.
Adjust frames per second and export the time-lapse imaging video.
